This is the homework 3!

#Problem 1
Load the NOAA data
```{r}
library(patchwork)
library(ggridges)
library(tidyverse)
library(p8105.datasets)
```

Check the number of rows and columns.
Check first 5 row of dataset to look variables.
```{r}
data("ny_noaa")
nrow(ny_noaa)
ncol(ny_noaa)
head(ny_noaa)
```
Check missing values in each variable
```{r}
colSums(is.na(ny_noaa))
```
The ny_noaa dataset contains 2,595,176 observations and 7 variables.

The dataset includes station ID (id), date (date), precipitation (prcp), snowfall (snow), snow depth (snwd), maximum temperature (tmax), and minimum temperature (tmin).Each row represents a weather observation for a station on a specific date.

There are no missing values in id or date.
Missing data are present in the weather variables, with 145,838 missing values in prcp, 381,221 in snow, 591,786 in snwd, 1,134,358 in tmax, and 1,134,420 in tmin.

Missing data are big issue in this dataset, especially for the temperature.


Separate date into year, month, and day.
Then check.
```{r}
ny_noaa =
  ny_noaa |>
  separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-")
ny_noaa
```

Ensure observations for temperature, precipitation, and snowfall are given in reasonable units.
Convert temperature to Celsius.
```{r}
ny_noaa =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )
```

For snowfall, what are the most commonly observed values? Why?
```{r}
ny_noaa =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(prcp = prcp / 10)

```
According to the data description, precipitation, maximum temperature, and minimum temperature were originally measured in tenths of their respective units.
I divided prcp, tmax, and tmin by 10 so that precipitation is measured in millimeters and temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.
snow and snwd were already measured in millimeters.


```{r}
ny_noaa |>
  count(snow) |>
  arrange(desc(n))

```
The most commonly observed snowfall value is 0 mm, with 2,008,508 observations.
I think because most days do not have snowfall.

Make a two-panel plot showing the average max temperature in January and in July in each station across years. Is there any observable / interpretable structure? Any outliers?

Keep January and July observations
```{r}
ny_noaa_jan_july =
  ny_noaa |>
  filter(month == "01" | month == "07")
```

Calculate average maximum temperature
In my first attempt, I got NaN values when calculating the mean because some stations had missing tmax values. So I used drop_na(tmax) before calculating the average maximum temperature.
```{r}
jan_july_tmax =
  ny_noaa_jan_july |>
  drop_na(tmax) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(mean_tmax = mean(tmax))
jan_july_tmax
```
Change year to numeric
```{r}
jan_july_tmax =
  jan_july_tmax |>
  mutate(year = as.numeric(year))
```

Plot average maximum temperature in January and July

```{r}
jan_july_tmax |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .5) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Maximum Temperature (C)"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(1981, 1990, 2000, 2010)
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Average maximum temperatures are much lower in January than in July.
Average temperatures in January range from -10°C to 10°C, while average temperatures in July range from 20°C to 30°C.
There are some outliers.A January value around -13°C and a July value around 14°C.


Make a two-panel plot showing (i) tmax vs tmin for the full dataset (note that a scatterplot may not be the best option); 

Remove missing temperature values
```{r}
tmax_tmin =
  ny_noaa |>
  drop_na(tmax, tmin)
```

Plot maximum and minimum temperature
```{r}
tmax_tmin_plot =
  tmax_tmin |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tmin, y = tmax)) +
  geom_hex() +
  labs(
    title = "Maximum vs Minimum Temperature",
    x = "Minimum Temperature (C)",
    y = "Maximum Temperature (C)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
and (ii) make a plot showing the distribution of snowfall values greater than 0 and less than 100 separately by year.

Keep snowfall values between 0 and 100 mm
Change year to a factor
```{r}
snowfall_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  filter(snow > 0, snow < 100) |>
  mutate(year = factor(year))
```

Plot snowfall distribution by year
```{r}
snowfall_plot =
  snowfall_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = snow, y = year)) +
  geom_density_ridges(scale = .85) +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Distribution by Year",
    x = "Snowfall (mm)",
    y = "Year"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Combine the two plots
```{r}
snowfall_plot + tmax_tmin_plot
```
